pr_title: fix(pacakging): fix cpu/memory metrics when running inside LXC container as systemd service
pr_body:
##### Summary

Fixes: #14238

The issue is that the [LXCFS proc](https://github.com/lxc/lxcfs#introduction) is not mounted [because of ProtectControlGroups=on](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/issues/14238#issuecomment-1380719725) which causes Netdata to track the host system and not the LXC container it's running in.

> to track the host system and not the LXC container it's running in.

That is impossible to "fix" completely because an LXC container is not a VM, so we are limited to LXCFC procfs.

A further improvement in this direction will be to disable plugins that collect host system metrics, which do not make sense to collect inside the LXC container (e.g. ZFS, KSM, etc). I am not going to do it in this PR.

---

This PR:

 - Updates Netdata systemd unit file: configures [LXCFS proc mounts](https://github.com/lxc/lxcfs#introduction).
 - Fixes RAM calculation when using ZFS (we should ignore ZFS ARC cache shrinkable size).
 - Fixes calculation of the number of processors in system-info.sh.

##### Test Plan

- install this branch in LXC container
- check CPU cores (number) and memory (ram, mem available) charts.

issue_context.title: [Bug]: Incorrect memory reporting while running in lxc container
issue_context.body:
### Bug description

Memory reporting is incorrect when agent is running inside of Proxmox LCX container under systemd and kernel 5.19 - instead of reporting LXC's memory it reports host's memory.

Actually this is not netdata's bug, the problem is that when option `ProtectSystem=full` is active, systemd mounts proc fs from the host - this might be a bug either in systemd or LXC related code in the Linux kernel, maybe even specific to only some Kernel versions (I didn't  research this deep yet).

### Expected behavior

Netdata should report container's RAM usage.

This could be achieved by adding additional option to `netdata.service` file:

`BindReadOnlyPaths=/proc:/proc:rbind`


### Steps to reproduce

1. Install netdata inside of LXC container running Proxmox under kernel 5.19
2. Run it and you will see host memory instead of container's.


### Installation method

kickstart.sh

comments:
Hi, @aldem. Thanks for opening the ticket!

> This could be achieved by
> BindReadOnlyPaths=/proc:/proc:rbind

I checked it and it is more complex than this. I assume it is not only memory, but the desired result is to monitor the container (from inside the container) in general. Using "BindReadOnlyPaths" solves the problem for memory (partially) and for CPUs.

I said "partially", because the memory is completely wrong if using ZFS (which is likely on Proxmox). We take into account ZFS ARC cache:

https://github.com/netdata/netdata/blob/b513888be389f92b2323d1bb3fdf55c22d4e4bad/collectors/proc.plugin/proc_meminfo.c#L161-L163

And regardless of the use of "BindReadOnlyPaths=/proc" 

- the kernel exposes hosts' ZFS metrics inside an LXC container (`/proc/spl/kstat/zfs/`). 
- also, `/proc/diskstats` returns hosts devices too.
- likely something else.

If I am not completely wrong, `/proc/diskstats` is anyway not virtualized, containers see all host devices in "default" configuration (with or without systemd magic) - thus I doubt we can do something here. I believe that ZFS is exposed due to same bug/feature - and I am not aware of any way to prevent or disable this.

However, there is a solution - if netdata detects (or explicitly signalled in configuration) that it is running inside of LXC container, it may omit diskstats and ZFS memory calculations just because inside of LXC this makes little sense. Unless, of course, someone wants to monitor host from inside of LXC (in docker?) - but then the default configuration (without using `BindReadOnlyPaths`) does the trick anyway.

Another option is to allow to explicitly specify during installation how to handle this case - this way installation script may create an overlay and use `BindReadOnlyPaths` if requested or (by default) installation inside LXC is detected.

From my point of view, proper memory metrics are quite important so we could disregard the rest (diskstats & ZFS in particular), for now at least.
>  it may **omit** diskstats and **ZFS memory** calculations

That is what `htop` does when [calculating memory usage](https://github.com/htop-dev/htop/blob/4d40680aa04370b06e9a2acd732f0be2ee6b6eba/linux/Platform.c#L362-L371)
Did some research. I am not sure, but I think `ProtectSystem=full` has nothing to do with the problem.

> If MountAPIVFS= is used, let's mount /sys, /proc, /dev and /run into the it, but only as a fallback if the user hasn't mounted something there already. These mounts are hence overridden by any other explicitly configured mounts.

[apivfs_table](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/5228c58ebe8fb77d579f333263986a0798299ab7/src/core/namespace.c#L101-L108) (includes `/proc`).

[Add those mounts](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/5228c58ebe8fb77d579f333263986a0798299ab7/src/core/namespace.c#L2303-L2307) from the table if [namespace_info_mount_apivfs()](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/5228c58ebe8fb77d579f333263986a0798299ab7/src/core/namespace.c#L1643-L1657) which results to true **if any**

```c
ns_info->protect_control_groups ||
ns_info->protect_kernel_tunables ||
ns_info->protect_proc != PROTECT_PROC_DEFAULT ||
ns_info->proc_subset != PROC_SUBSET_ALL
```

Any of the following options results in mounting host's `/proc`: 

- `ProtectControlGroups`
- `ProtectKernelTunables`
- `ProtectProc` (any non-default value)
- `ProcSubset` (any non-default value)


In our case it is [ProtectControlGroups=on](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/blob/5980b18ecd0a83d91c783bca597da7fb4156ce19/system/netdata.service.in#L69).
I checked `/proc/mounts` w/ and w/o enabled `ProtectControlGroups`. This is the difference @aldem:

```go
lxcfs /proc/cpuinfo fuse.lxcfs rw,nosuid,nodev,relatime,user_id=0,group_id=0,allow_other 0 0
lxcfs /proc/diskstats fuse.lxcfs rw,nosuid,nodev,relatime,user_id=0,group_id=0,allow_other 0 0
lxcfs /proc/loadavg fuse.lxcfs rw,nosuid,nodev,relatime,user_id=0,group_id=0,allow_other 0 0
lxcfs /proc/meminfo fuse.lxcfs rw,nosuid,nodev,relatime,user_id=0,group_id=0,allow_other 0 0
lxcfs /proc/stat fuse.lxcfs rw,nosuid,nodev,relatime,user_id=0,group_id=0,allow_other 0 0
lxcfs /proc/swaps fuse.lxcfs rw,nosuid,nodev,relatime,user_id=0,group_id=0,allow_other 0 0
lxcfs /proc/uptime fuse.lxcfs rw,nosuid,nodev,relatime,user_id=0,group_id=0,allow_other 0 0
lxcfs /sys/devices/system/cpu/online fuse.lxcfs rw,nosuid,nodev,relatime,user_id=0,group_id=0,allow_other 0 0
```

^^ These entries are missing **when enabled**. It explains why ZFS stats are exposed from inside the container. See [LXCFS](https://github.com/lxc/lxcfs#introduction).

This issue has been mentioned on the **Netdata Community Forums**. There might be relevant details there:

https://community.netdata.cloud/t/incorrect-available-memory-values-with-lxd-containers/3604/13
Fixed in #14255
Just realized that we have a problem with loadavg after #14255. Load average virtualization is disabled by default in LXCFS (`-l, --enable-loadavg Enable loadavg virtualization`) - it means that all [loadavg alarms](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/blob/master/health/health.d/load.conf) will be active because the calculation is based on the number of processors. 🤷‍♂️ how to fix that properly.

We are calling this function before to start main loop,  but we are defining `ff` as `static` and we are not closing it, I suggest to avoid memory leak the following modifications:

1. Remove `static` for cited variable.
2. If we have success to open file, before to return call `procfile_close`. We have an example [here](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/blob/cbbd338cad8848064a72a579c152e56a3975b96b/collectors/apps.plugin/apps_plugin.c#L616-L666).

Except for this small improvement, the PR is running as expected.
